parameters.name: DeviceName
parameters.description:
The device name to which the custom topic belongs.

><notice>For open-source MQTT managed products and devices, and MQTT cloud gateway products and devices, if the **Topic** is a custom topic and **ScopeType** is set to **DEVICE**, this parameter is required.
></notice>

parameters.name: IotInstanceId
parameters.description:
The instance ID. You can view the **ID** of the current instance on the **Instance Overview** page in the IoT Platform console.

><notice>
- If this ID value exists, you must specify it. Otherwise, the call fails.
- If the **Instance Overview** page or **ID** value is not available, you do not need to specify this parameter.

></notice>

For more information about instances, see [Instance overview](~~356505~~).

parameters.name: ProductKey
parameters.description:
The **ProductKey** of the product to which the custom topic belongs.

><notice>For open-source MQTT managed products and devices, and MQTT cloud gateway products and devices, this parameter is required.
></notice>

parameters.name: ScopeType
parameters.description:
The scope of the custom topic subscription. Valid values:

- **PRODUCT**: product scope. The subscription applies to all devices under the product. You must also specify **ProductKey**.
- **DEVICE**: device scope. The subscription applies to a specified device under the product. You must also specify **DeviceName**.

><notice>For open-source MQTT managed products and devices, and MQTT cloud gateway products and devices, if the **Topic** is a custom topic, this parameter is required.
></notice>

parameters.name: Topic
parameters.description:
The specific topic to be applied to the rules engine. The format is generally: `/${productKey}/${deviceName}/topicShortName`. In this format, `${productKey}` is the **ProductKey** of the product to which the device belongs, `${deviceName}` is the name of the specific device, and `topicShortName` is the remaining part of the topic.

- The format of a basic communication topic or Thing Specification Language model communication topic is generally: `/${productKey}/${deviceName}/topicShortName`. The `${deviceName}` can be replaced with the wildcard `+` to represent all device names under the product. Valid values of `topicShortName`:

    - `/thing/event/property/post`: property messages reported by devices.
    - `/thing/event/${tsl.event.identifier}/post`: event messages reported by devices. The `${}` contains the event identifier in the product Thing Specification Language model.
    - `/thing/lifecycle`: device lifecycle change messages.
    - `/thing/downlink/reply/message`: result messages of device responses to cloud commands.
    - `/thing/list/found`: messages reported by gateways about discovered sub-devices.
    - `/thing/topo/lifecycle`: device topology relationship change messages.
    - `/thing/event/property/history/post`: historical property messages reported by devices.
    - `/thing/event/${tsl.event.identifier}/history/post`: historical event messages reported by devices. The `${}` contains the event identifier in the product Thing Specification Language model.
    - `/ota/upgrade`: device OTA update status notification messages.
    - `/ota/version/post`: device OTA module version number reporting messages.
    - `/thing/deviceinfo/update`: device tag change messages.

    The OTA update batch status notification topic is also a basic communication topic. The format is: `/${productKey}/${packageId}/${jobId}/ota/job/status`. In this format, `${packageId}` is over-the-air update package ID, and `${jobId}` is over-the-air update batch ID.
- A custom topic is: `/${productKey}/${deviceName}/user/#`, such as: `/${productKey}/${deviceName}/user/get`.

  Call the [QueryProductTopic](~~69647~~) operation to view all custom topic categories under a product.

    When specifying a custom topic, you can use the wildcards `+` and `#`.
    - `${deviceName}` can be replaced with the wildcard `+` to represent all devices under the product.
    - Subsequent fields can use `/user/#`, where `#` represents all levels after the `/user` level.
    
- The device status change notification topic is: `/as/mqtt/status/${productKey}/${deviceName}`.

 You can directly use the wildcard `+` to represent status change notifications for all devices under the product.

For more information about wildcards, see [Wildcards in topic categories](~~85539~~).

For more information about topic data formats, see [Data formats](~~73736~~).

><notice>For open-source MQTT managed products and devices, and MQTT cloud gateway products and devices, only custom topics, device status change notification topics, and device lifecycle change topics are supported. For more information about custom topics, see the messaging description. If you specify a custom topic, you must also specify **ScopeType** and **ProductKey**. If **ScopeType** is set to **DEVICE**, you must also specify **DeviceName**.
></notice>
